claims.text: Sarcoidosis on corticosteroids: alendronate or another bisphosphonate may be the treatment of choice to prevent steroid-induced osteoporosis in at-risk patients (eg, older).
claims.quote: Alendronate or another bisphosphonate may be the treatment of choice for prevention of corticosteroid-induced osteoporosis in people at risk (eg, older patients).

claims.text: Calcium/vitamin D supplements risk hypercalcemia (granulomas make active vitamin D):
claims.quote: Using supplemental calcium or vitamin D risks hypercalcemia due to endogenous production of active vitamin D (1, 25 dihydroxy vitamin D) by sarcoidal granulomas.

claims.text: serum and 24-h urine calcium should be normal before starting them.
claims.quote: Serum and 24-hour urinary calcium measurements should be normal before starting such supplements.

claims.text: Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (prednisone ≥ 7.5 mg/day equivalent with low BMD):
claims.quote: FOSAMAX is indicated for the treatment of glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis in men and women receiving glucocorticoids in a daily dosage equivalent to 7.5 mg or greater of prednisone and who have low bone mineral density

claims.text: 5 mg PO daily; 10 mg daily in postmenopausal women not on estrogen.
claims.quote: Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis: 5 mg daily; or 10 mg daily in postmenopausal women not receiving estrogen.
FOSAMAX is not recommended for patients with creatinine clearance less than 35 mL/min .

claims.text: Correct hypocalcemia (and vitamin D deficiency) before starting.
claims.quote: Hypocalcemia must be corrected before initiating therapy with FOSAMAX [see Contraindications (4) ] . Other disorders affecting mineral metabolism (such as vitamin D deficiency) should also be effectively treated.

claims.text: Calcium, antacids and other multivalent-cation drugs block absorption: wait at least one-half hour after alendronate before any other oral drug.
claims.quote: Co-administration of FOSAMAX and calcium, antacids, or oral medications containing multivalent cations will interfere with absorption of FOSAMAX. Therefore, instruct patients to wait at least one-half hour after taking FOSAMAX before taking any other oral medications.
Use caution when co-prescribing aspirin/nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs that may worsen gastrointestinal irritation.
